text:
mia: Heads-up — found a class of broken in-page links after we merged the docs migration. Anchors with underscores (e.g., `#api_keys`) jump to top instead of the section.

mia: Quick repro: open https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/security then click the left nav link to 'API keys' which points to `/guides/security#api_keys`. Page loads but doesn't scroll.

ryan: I can reproduce. Looks like the parser turns `api_keys` into `api-keys` in the generated id but our old links use underscores.

nina: That's annoying. Is this Docusaurus' slugify change again or did mkdocs behave differently? We have a mix in the repo for a while.

tyler: It's the slugifier. Newer Docusaurus normalizes punctuation and underscores to hyphens. Two choices: update all incoming links to hyphens (huge), or add explicit IDs for the affected headings. Small script can scan for `#` links that contain `_` and map to actual rendered ids.

mia: I ran a grep and found ~12 pages linking with underscores. Most are in guides and examples. I'll open a follow-up PR that patches the top 10 most visible ones with explicit header IDs so anchors remain stable: e.g. `### API keys {#api_keys}`.

ryan: Could also add a short middleware that rewrites `#api_keys` to `#api-keys` client-side as a stopgap. But I prefer content-level fixes + a note in migration docs.

nina: For the ones that are code examples (where underscores are inside code fences) we need to be careful: markdown codefence language hints like ```js cause some renderers to create odd headings when someone pastes `### Usage_example()`. Suggest we escape the parens/backticks in examples.

mia: Example patch I will use:```markdown
### API keys {#api_keys}
Use these keys for server-to-server requests.

```js
// Old snippet that showed inline anchor-like text
const creds = { api_key: process.env.API_KEY } // keep underscore in code
```
```
Note: keep underscore in code blocks, only the heading gets explicit id.

tyler: Add a line to docs/migration/docusaurus.md explaining underscore->hyphen slug changes + recommended remediation (explicit IDs or regex-based replace).

mia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4321 — patches 9 files, adds migration note, and includes a tiny script `scripts/fix-underscore-anchors.sh` that prints a diff so reviewers can see old vs new.

docs-bot: CI started for PR 4321 — linkcheck queueing.

nina: Reviewed and left two small comments: 1) prefer `<!-- keep-anchor: api_keys -->` style comment above heading instead of inline `{#...}` for readability, 2) escape backticks in the SDK example wrapper.

mia: Updated per review. Using HTML comment keeps markdown cleaner and avoids odd linter complaints. Patch now uses:
```markdown
<!-- keep-anchor: api_keys -->
### API keys
```
Then our docs build step runs a tiny preprocessor that converts those comments to explicit IDs before render.

ryan: Smart move. That preprocessor also makes the cleanup PR easier (we can remove comments later if we standardize config).

docs-bot: Linkcheck completed: 1 warning (external redirect), 0 failures. Preview: https://deploy-preview-4321--docs.redwood.ai/guides/security — build id 2026-03-22-09:12

tyler: Merged PR 4321. Confirmed the nav link now jumps properly.

mia: Added a short entry to the migration notes and opened issue #210 to track a future global rewrite of old underscore anchors (regex-based) if we decide to pick that path.

nina: Thanks everyone. If you find other underscore anchors, drop them here or tag me and I'll triage.

tyler: One follow-up: let's add a test to the linkcheck job that fails when an internal link points to a non-existent id (we currently only warn). I'll open a tiny CI PR for that.

mia: Sounds good — can close once CI test lands.
